cards.title: Growing crisis
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Crucial for Pakistan Affairs and Governance papers covering demographics, socioeconomic planning, and federal resource distribution via the NFC.
cards.summary: Pakistan's National Population Council has declared rapid population growth a national emergency. The 2023 census showed an annual growth rate of 2.55 percent, which places intense strain on public infrastructure and basic amenities. Planning officials note that the National Finance Commission formula gives population an 82 percent weight, unintentionally creating a disincentive for provinces to curb fertility. Addressing this challenge requires better tracking of contraceptives, rural clinic staffing, and rewarding provinces that enhance family planning and female education.
key_facts: Pakistan's 2023 national census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55 percent.
The National Population Council's executive committee declared rapid population growth a national emergency.
The National Finance Commission (NFC) resource distribution formula assigns an 82 percent weight to population.

vocab.meaning: a device, drug, or method used to prevent pregnancy

text: AN emergency can be judged by the speed with which it draws an effective response. The National Population Council’s executive committee has declared rapid population growth a national emergency . But Pakistan has been warned about this crisis for decades, with little to show for it.

People still struggle to obtain reproductive healthcare, clinics run short of contraceptives, and millions of couples lack the information and services needed to plan families. The 2023 census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55pc, placing further pressure on schools, hospitals, housing, jobs and water supplies. The state cannot keep announcing plans while failing to provide basic services.

One key decision taken at the meeting was to improve the tracking of contraceptive supplies. But collecting data is only the first step. Provinces must ensure that clinics are adequately equipped, healthcare workers are trained and family planning services reach remote and neglected communities. Religious scholars can also help address misconceptions about birth spacing, particularly by explaining its benefits for mothers and children.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has raised another important issue: the National Finance Commission formula , which gives population an 82pc weight in the distribution of provincial resources. His concern that the formula may reward population growth deserves attention.

However, simply giving provinces more money for reducing birth rates could create fresh problems. Provinces with larger, poorer populations already face greater demands for schools, hospitals and other services. Cutting their share would only make these problems worse.

Instead, the government should consider rewarding provinces that improve access to family planning, girls’ education and maternal healthcare, while ensuring that funding reflects their actual needs. Above all, the authorities must recognise that population planning is about helping people make informed choices, not merely bringing down numbers.
Calling population growth a national emergency is easy. Ensuring that the response reaches the people who need it is the real challenge.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Muddled hierarchy
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Directly relevant to Governance and Constitutional Law questions regarding the 26th and 27th Amendments and judicial restructuring.
cards.summary: The Federal Constitutional Court celebrated its first anniversary amid unresolved questions about judicial primacy between it and the Supreme Court. The 26th Amendment of October 2024 initially set up constitutional benches, but the 27th Amendment quickly split them into a separate court. The FCC claims its decisions bind all judicial forums, while Supreme Court leadership argues both bodies are coordinate courts. This ongoing institutional friction highlights deep administrative fractures within Pakistan's reformed legal structure.
key_facts: The 26th Constitutional Amendment was passed in October 2024 to create constitutional benches within the Supreme Court.
The 27th Constitutional Amendment established the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) as an entirely separate judicial entity.
Two of the Supreme Court's senior-most judges resigned in protest on the day the 27th Amendment became law.

vocab.meaning: the state of being first in importance, rank, or authority
equal in rank, authority, or importance

text: THE Federal Constitutional Court marked its first anniversary on Friday with a commemorative stamp. Speaking on the occasion, its chief justice remarked on how fleeting the year had been.
Litigants, lawyers and the judges of the Supreme Court might have described it differently.

A year after the 27th Amendment rewrote the structure of the country’s judiciary, one of the most basic questions raised by the new order remains unanswered: which court, the FCC or the SC, has the final word? This was, perhaps, bound to happen. Critics had foreseen problems in the short and hurried route the government took from the 26th to the 27th Amendment .

In October 2024, the 26th Amendment carved constitutional benches out of the SC, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission in which judges no longer held a majority. Critics warned then that the independence of the judiciary was at stake.

Barely a year later, and in evident haste, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law. Thousands of cases were soon transferred to the FCC, and the SC was stripped of its constitutional jurisdiction.

What has followed has seemed less a division of labour than a contest for primacy. Last December, the FCC held that its rulings bind all courts, including the SC, but that the latter’s do not bind the FCC. In May, Chief Justice Yahya Afridi pushed back, ruling that the two are coordinate courts, neither an appellate forum over the other. Last month, the FCC rebuked an SC bench for revisiting a matter the FCC considered settled, raising concerns over judicial discipline. The sparring shows no sign of stopping.
The text of the amendment arguably favours the FCC, while the SC relies on the overall constitutional scheme to assert its position. That both positions can be argued is precisely the problem.

Two hasty amendments have created an ambiguity that leaves the two courts defining their relationship through pointed observations in their judgments. The costs are borne by litigants, whose cases risk being shuttled between forums. The FCC, meanwhile, has worked with seven judges against a sanctioned strength of 13. And its order barring the Peshawar High Court from hearing petitions on emergency and governor’s rule in KP has pushed citizens away from a court closer to home.

Since parliament created this ambiguity, it must now resolve it. The jurisdiction of the two courts and a mechanism for settling disputes between them should be spelt out in law, not left to judges to fight over.
Lastly, the judiciary’s structure is not its only problem. As long as its independence remains in doubt, it will struggle to win public confidence.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Islamabad hosts foreign dignitaries for two-day ECO ministerial meeting
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: ECO multilateral diplomacy and regional economic integration are frequent topics in CSS Current Affairs and International Relations papers.
cards.summary: Pakistan hosted the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers in Islamabad. Delegations from ten member states, along with officials from the SCO and OIC, arrived to attend the two-day conference. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar underscored Pakistan's dedication to regional connectivity and common economic development.
key_facts: Pakistan hosted the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers in Islamabad.
The ECO consists of 10 member states: Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic, and Uzbekistan.
Dignitaries attending included SCO Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda and OIC Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed.

vocab.meaning: long and careful discussions before reaching a decision

text: Foreign dignitaries arrived in Islamabad on Sunday as Pakistan hosts the two-day 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers, starting today .
Currently, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic and Uzbekistan are part of the ECO.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner in honour of the foreign ministers and heads of delegations of the member states in Islamabad ahead of the meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said on social media.
He warmly welcomed the delegates and wished them productive deliberations while highlighting the close bonds among ECO member states, the FO said.
Addressing the gathering, DPM Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “regional cooperation and advancing shared aspirations for peace, progress and prosperity”.

Alongside the visiting delegations, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Parliamentary Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary, representatives of the ECO secretariat, members of the diplomatic corps, and senior officials of the foreign ministry were also in attendance, FO added.

Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Musa Kulaklikaya, and Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy FM Kairat Erkinovich Tursunkulov are among those in Islamabad for the meeting.
Azeri Deputy FM Elnur Mammadov, Kazakh Deputy FM Arman Issagaliyev, and Turkmenistan’s FM Rashid Meredov also arrived in the federal capital today.
At night, Iran’s FM Abbas Araghchi also landed in Islamabad for the moot, Iran’s state media reported.
Upon his arrival, Meredov, who is also the deputy chairman of Turkmenistan’s cabinet of ministers, was received by Pakistan’s Ambassador to Turkmenistan and other officials, the FO said.
The foreign minister of Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Tahsin Ertugruloglu, had landed in Pakistan on Saturday for the meeting.
According to APP , incumbent ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan chaired a meeting on the draft agenda of the 30th ECO-COM.

This gathering of senior officials from ECO member states was set to review the organisation’s activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers.

Monday’s ministerial meeting will be chaired by DPM Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies.

Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”, the FO said in a statement on Saturday.

It said Pakistan’s chairmanship would focus on strengthening regional connectivity and integration, deepening partnerships and promoting collective efforts for economic prosperity and sustainable development.
The chairmanship would also provide an opportunity to strengthen the ECO’s role as a platform for regional cooperation, dialogue and economic collaboration, it added.
According to the FO, Pakistan also aims to position itself as a regional connectivity hub, facilitate logistics supply chains and help shape the agenda for regional trade.

The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said.
Dar meets ECO, OIC, CICA heads
On the sidelines of the meeting, DPM Dar met Ambassador Majeed, FO said.

Dar underscored the importance of strengthening “regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration” within the ECO region. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to hosting the ECO Summit in 2027, the FO said.
He also appreciated the ECO secretariat’s efforts in advancing the agenda of the organisation, and its support for Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship.

“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s excellent arrangements, hospitality and coordination for the 30th ECO-COM and congratulated Pakistan on its upcoming chairmanship and hosting of the ECO-COM and ECO Summit in 2027, reflecting the importance Pakistan attaches to regionalism and multilateral cooperation,” the statement said.

It added that both sides reaffirmed the importance of close coordination during Pakistan’s chairmanship “to ensure effective implementation of agreed initiatives and advance shared goals of regional development and prosperity”.
DPM Dar also held a meeting with the OIC secretary general, welcoming him on his first visit to Islamabad since assuming office this year, the FO said.

He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening the OIC as a unified and effective voice of the Muslim Ummah” and assured Ahmed of Pakistan’s continued support and cooperation in advancing the OIC’s objectives.

“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts during the Iran-US conflict to promote peace and stability in the region. He also commended Pakistan’s active role in the OIC, including its contributions through COMSTECH to promoting scientific and technological cooperation among member states,” the FO said.

Both sides agreed to maintain close cooperation within the OIC, while also reiterating “their steadfast support for the peoples of Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir and the realisation of their right to self-determination”, it added.

The deputy premier also met with the secretary general of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev, where he reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for CICA and its efforts to promote peace, security and stability in Asia through dialogue and confidence-building measures.

Hajiyev appreciated Pakistan’s constructive efforts in promoting dialogue and de-escalation. He also thanked Pakistan “for its warm hospitality and excellent arrangements” for the council meeting, the FO said.

Separately, the ECO secretary general also met Deputy FM Tursunkulov to discuss Kyrgyzstan’s “contributions and ECO’s work in a range of areas including trade, energy, industry and tourism cooperation”, he said.

cards.title: Organised rackets
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Highly pertinent for International Relations, Security, and Governance topics regarding transnational crime and compliance with international standards.
cards.summary: Marking the International Day against Transnational Organised Crime, observers highlighted Pakistan's persistent vulnerabilities as a source and transit hub for illicit operations. Weak border enforcement, economic distress, and climate catastrophes continue to facilitate exploitation by fraud networks and human traffickers. Pakistan holds poor standings on international crime tracking indices and requires systemic institutional reforms. Curbing financial fraud, digital scams, and cybercrime requires dismantling systemic impunity and aligning with global anti-crime conventions.
key_facts: The Global Organised Crime Index 2025 ranked Pakistan 45th out of 193 nations.
Pakistan was placed on Tier 2 of the United States State Department's 2024 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report.
The theme for the International Day against Transnational Organised Crime was 'Follow the money. Stop organised fraud'.

vocab.meaning: a group of individuals or organizations combined to promote a common, often illicit, interest
exemption from punishment or freedom from the injurious consequences of an action

text: ON the International Day against Transnational Organised Crime, observed today, Pakistan finds itself in a tight spot. Socioeconomic and climate challenges, porous borders and poor institutional scrutiny have made the country a supplier and a transit centre for organised crime activities. The inability to lower factors fuelling the menace continues to be a serious indictment of the state’s policies and crime control measures. The Global Organised Crime Index 2025 placed Pakistan on the 45th position out of 193 countries; it was on ‘Tier 2’ of the 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report by the US State Department. In this setting, where criminal syndicates impede justice and economic progress, this year’s theme, “Follow the money. Stop organised fraud”, puts the focus on the need for a multi-layered approach.

Deepening poverty and climate disasters offer opportunities for criminal networks to exploit vulnerable individuals. As financial commodities, fake tech supplies and Ponzi schemes proliferate, unsuspecting citizens and authentic technology enterprises become increasingly vulnerable. Consequently, surging incidents of identity theft, impersonation, caller ID spoofing, and more, show that cybercrime is another significant threat. Alongside these, fraud, money laundering, and corruption facilitate the accumulation of illegal fortunes, create economic disruption and erode institutional integrity, serving as primary enablers of organised crime. Pakistan needs a drastic overhaul that, based on the practices and procedures mentioned in global conventions, dismantles the culture of impunity as well as holds offenders and their promoters to account. For cohesive crime databases, arrest and conviction numbers along with transnational links must remain consistent. Departments, such as the FIA, should be enabled to tackle influential quarters, choke root causes and ensure equal access to justice. Organised crime operators — from scam centres, human traffickers to money launderers — must be dealt with across the board.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Contested frontier
cards.author: Aamir Khan
cards.why: Essential historical background for International Relations and Regional Affairs papers discussing Sino-Indian rivalries and boundary treaties.
cards.summary: The Sino-Indian border dispute has its origins in ambiguous boundaries drawn during the British colonial era. In the Western Sector, British mapping shifted repeatedly regarding Aksai Chin, leaving the frontier neither legally delimited nor physically demarcated. In the Eastern Sector, British India and Tibetan officials agreed on the McMahon Line during the 1913-14 Simla Conference without Chinese ratification. These unresolved imperial cartographic legacies directly underpin contemporary clashes in areas such as Galwan.
key_facts: British control over Kashmir was formally established in 1846.
The British proposed a boundary to China in 1899 allocating a substantial part of Aksai Chin to China.
The Simla Conference took place in 1913-14, where British India and Tibet agreed to the McMahon Line without Chinese approval.

vocab.meaning: the theoretical or written determination of a boundary line in a treaty
the physical marking of a boundary on the actual ground

text: IN a new movie starring Salman Khan, Bollywood has smartly invested in a tale that can reap financial benefits by inflaming the emotions of Indians still traumatised by 1962. But behind the Galwan incident of 2020 lies a tale that is far more fascinating than the movie itself: the riveting story of the Sino-Indian border.

But let us rewind first to the 19th century, when Russia and Britain were fearful that their nemesis was advancing towards an area stretching from present-day Afghanistan to Tibet. Kashmir had come under British control in 1846, but it was not clear where the boundary lay between Ladakh and Tibet. A map drawn by W.H. Johnson suggested that Aksai Chin lay within Kashmir, but later, in 1899, the British proposed a different boundary to China, which showed that a big chunk of Aksai Chin belonged to the latter. In short, there was neither delimitation (verbal or written agreement) nor demarcation (marking the line on the ground) of the border between China and British India in the Western Sector.

Enter the Eastern Sector. Here, again, no boundary existed between China and British India, but the latter did adhere to the so-called Inner and Outer Lines. However, in 1913-14, the momentous Simla Conference was held, attended by representatives of British India, China and Tibet. Britain proposed dividing Tibet into Inner and Outer zones. A weak China asked its envoy to leave and thus, in a moment of great wisdom, saved itself from calamity. However, Tibet, which was claimed by China on the basis of both international treaties and custom, and Britain did sign an agreement, a secret part of which specified the McMahon Line (MML) as the border between India and Chinese Tibet. The border was thus delimited but not demarcated, and was not agreed upon by China. The line was drawn by a marker whose width on the map would cover many mountain crests.

Move forward to 1959. By now, India had gained independence, China had moved from weakness to strength and re-established control over Tibet, the Dalai Lama had fled Tibet to seek refuge in India, Nehru was firmly in command of India, and had extended India’s control up to the MML, but there was still no boundary in the Western Sector. And China had been suggesting to India that they stabilise the border, to no avail.
Nehru completely misread what China wanted.

Nehru was a great leader with two minor blemishes: he ruined India’s economy and he ruined India’s relations with China. He now made three pivotal blunders which would have a long-term impact. First, he completely misread what China wanted. China wanted to settle the border with India around the MML, with one proviso: negotiations on the MML should be held afresh. Why? Remember, the MML was agreed upon by the British and the Tibetans. If China agreed to the MML, it would have to admit that Tibet in 1913-14 was independent.

Second, Aksai Chin, some 15,000sq miles of barren land, was of no use to India but was vital to China because of the presence of a road which connects Tibet with Xinjiang. China would have ceded the Nor­th-East Frontier Agency’s (NEFA) 40,000sq miles to India but would never have accepted Indian control over Aksai Chin.

Third, in one of the most self-harming moves, Nehru initiated his infamous ‘For­w­ard Policy.’ Remember, the borders in both sectors were not demarcated. And we are talking about some of the highest, roughest landscapes here. Nehru ordered Indian troops to move forward and start occupying the spaces in between the Chinese outposts, and even fire upon the Chinese to vacate their posts. The Ind­ian generals warned Nehru aga­inst this madness, but to no avail. A senior Chi­n­ese diplomat told me, “they started cutting up our soldiers to pieces and we did not move a muscle.”

On Oct 20, 1962, the Chinese, fed up, attacked across both sectors. The Indian 7 Brigade dissolved into thin air. The war was over as soon as it began. The Chinese occupied NEFA, and, in one of the most astonishing moments in world history, declared that they would unilaterally withdraw.

The war left Nehru’s reputation in tatters. It ‘gifted’ Kashmir to Pakistan on a silver platter, and led India into making a U-turn and accepting the West’s military aid. The war also sowed the seeds of an en-mity which was many times more prono­unced in an India where the population was never told the truth than in China, where much saner minds had been in command.

In 2026, when Salman Khan’s movie on the Galwan incident of 2020 is released to an emotional population, the latter will not be told that it was Nehru’s hubris, intransigence and folly which had led to this state of affairs.
History can be more fascinating than Bollywood movies.
The writer has a First-class degree in history from Oxford and has worked in China as a diplomat.
aamir3123@gmail.com
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: Trilateral security alliances and defence partnerships are critical to questions on Middle East diplomacy and Pakistan's strategic posture.
cards.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir shared the top spot in the 500 Most Influential Muslims rankings. The publication by Jordan's Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre recognized their role in the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The collective pact unites Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye in a mutual security arrangement.
key_facts: The Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), based in Amman, Jordan, has published the annual list since 2009.
The top spot was shared between the leadership of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye due to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
The mutual defence pact unites Saudi financial strength, Turkish manufacturing and technology, and Pakistan's military forces.

vocab.meaning: very complicated or detailed
the reduction of the intensity of a conflict or tension

text: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top spot in the latest edition of the world’s 500 most influential Muslims, alongside the Saudi king and crown prince and the Turkish president.

The rankings have been compiled by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), a research institute based in Amman, Jordan. It has been publishing an annual report titled “The 500 Most Influential Muslims” since 2009, recognising and highlighting individuals who have made significant contributions to Muslim communities.
This is the first time that the list features multiple names for the top rank, recognising the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, according to the edition.

“While this unified top spot features five individuals, it is actually divided into three shared entries that represent a massive shift in how Muslim nations are working together to protect one another. The main reason for this historic decision is the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” the edition said.

It added, “This mutual-defence pact unites the immense wealth of Saudi Arabia, the advanced tech and manufacturing of Turkiye, and the powerful military strength of Pakistan into a collective alliance.
“Modelled on a ‘one for all, all for one’ approach to security, this pact has completely reshaped regional politics.”

The report also acknowledged that “over the past year, Pakistan has navigated an intricate set of economic stabilisation challenges, regional security pressures, and major-power diplomatic balancing acts”.

It noted that Islamabad engaged in “regional shuttle diplomacy” in the Middle East to advocate for de-escalation, “even as domestic energy markets faced immediate pressures via elevated import costs and emergency fuel conservation measures”.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar posted about the development on X, saying, “A moment of gratitude for every Pakistani.”
He added, “From Marka-i-Haq to global diplomacy, they walked this journey together. This honour is a tribute to the sacrifices of our martyrs and the unity of our nation.”

Following the leaders of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, at the fourth and fifth place in the list are Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei and Jordan’s King Abdullah II, respectively.

Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani is ranked at number six while United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al-Nahyan has been ranked at number 12. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Saeed El-Sisi is at number 22.
Pakistani Scholar Sheikh Muhammad Taqi Usmani has been listed as the seventh most influential Muslim, while Scholar Maulana Tariq Jamil is ranked at 32.
Footballer Mohamed Salah is ranked at 39.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas is listed at number 45, followed by Syrian Interim President Ahmed Al-Sharaa at the 46th place.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is listed as the 49th most influential Muslim in the list.
Honourable mentions in politics include Hamas Chief Khalil Al-Hayya, former prime minister Imran Khan, London Mayor Sadiq Khan and American Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed .

Similarly, honourable mentions in the “Social Issues, Science, Arts & Culture, Media and Sports” category include Jordan’s Queen Rania Al-Abdullah, British composer Sami Yusuf, Palestinian journalist Bisan Owda, British-American broadcaster and journalist Mehdi Hasan and Egyptian comedian Bassem Youssef.
Every year, the RISSC also names two people as Man of the Year and Woman of the Year.

This year, Palestinian paediatrician Dr Hussam Abu Safiya has been named as the Man of the Year. He is described as “a doctor who refused to abandon his patients, buried his son and returned to the wards, and has now spent more than six hundred days in Israeli custody without charge or trial”.

Under Israel’s invasion of Gaza, he documented attacks on medical facilities and appealed to the international community to protect Gaza’s health infrastructure. “A man with no army, no office and no freedom has done more than most governments to remind the world what courage and integrity look like,” the report says.
Minab school attack survivor Fatemeh Zahra Sheikhabadi has been honoured as the Woman of the Year.
On Feb 28, a US missile struck an elementary girls school in Iran’s Minab, killing over 150 people, including over 100 children.

After surviving the US strikes on her school, Sheikhabadi travelled to Geneva and addressed the UN Human Rights Council, urging world leaders to “hear the voices of the children of Minab”, the report says.

“She is honoured not as a symbol of a war, but as herself: a girl who lost her friends and her teachers on an ordinary morning, and who lived to tell their story so that it would not be lost with them,” the report added.

cards.title: US has suggested Kyiv cede land for Nato entry: Zelensky
cards.author: AFP
cards.why: Crucial for understanding diplomatic negotiations, territorial sovereignty issues, and shifting security architectures in the Russia-Ukraine war.
cards.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed that US representatives suggested Kyiv surrender occupied territory to Moscow in return for NATO entry. Discussions in Abu Dhabi featuring US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff concluded without a formal agreement. In Dublin, European states chose five countries to participate directly in upcoming peace talks. Zelensky maintained that Ukrainian voters must decide whether to approve any settlement.
key_facts: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held discussions with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky following talks in Abu Dhabi.
European nations selected five countries—France, Germany, Italy, the UK, and Poland—to join future talks.
President Zelensky asserted that Ukraine will not legally recognise Russian control over seized territories.

vocab.meaning: to give up control or ownership of land to another power

text: KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released on Saturday, saying his country’s relationship with the Western alliance is “back on the agenda.”

Zelensky also warned of the dangers of Moscow’s push to redraw “influence” in Europe and said the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign. Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelensky on Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough. Nego­tiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries join future talks on ending the war.

In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries — France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland — to send representatives to the talks. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said, adding: “After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go.” He beli­eved “Nato is back on the agenda” as Ukraine — with almost five years of combat experience — can make the alliance “stronger.” Nato and Washington have not yet commented.
Kyiv seeks guarantees

Kyiv — seeking post-war support for its army — was in talks on “specific” guarantees from Western cou­ntries, Zelensky said. Before agreeing to anything, he added, he would ask Ukrainians “do we accept it or not?”. He insisted Ukra­ine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow’s troops as Russian.

Russia has consistently said Kyiv joining Nato is a red line and in 2022 launched its invasion, saying the West planned to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance. Putin has for years logged grievances at Nato. Meeting US envoys this week, he ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine. And throughout the negotiations, the Kremlin has ruled out wider ceasefires. But Putin earlier this week proposed a “humanitarian” mission to the eastern town of Kostya­ntynivka — which Moscow annou­nced it had seized in summer but where Kyiv says fighting continues.

Zelensky said this was a ploy to get Kyiv to withdraw from the embattled city and open the road to more settlements in the Donetsk region. If Ukraine gave up Kostyantynivka, “their next steps will be our other cities in Donbas. That is the thinking behind this idea”, he added.
Moscow’s troops have inched westwards but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow, Zelensky said, had also rejected an energy ceasefire at the Abu Dhabi talks.
‘First, end the war’

Russia has tried to reframe negotiations on ending the war — Europe’s worst since WWII — into a conversation on the continent’s wider security. In 2021, before its Ukraine invasion, Moscow issued an ultimatum to the West to pull back Nato troops from eastern Europe. This week, Moscow’s chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said the Kremlin’s aim now was for a “new, modern Yalta” — referring to the 1945 conference in which Western leaders divided Europe with Joseph Stalin.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Sindh cotton experiment faces winter test
cards.author: Amjad Mahmood
cards.why: Highlights innovative climate adaptation by farmers and off-season agricultural practices vital for Pakistan's cotton value chain.
cards.summary: Growers in lower Sindh have begun sowing cotton in November to adapt to shifting climate pressures. Planting early into tomato beds after the paddy harvest allows the crop to avoid extreme summer temperatures and severe pest strikes. Experts from the Central Cotton Research Institute in Sakrand are tracking these experimental fields. Successful winter maturation could provide local textile spinners with domestic lint months earlier than usual.
key_facts: Farmers in the coastal Sindh districts of Thatta and Sujawal started cotton sowing in the second week of November.
Standard cotton sowing runs from February to March in Sindh and May to June in Punjab.
The off-season planting strategy aims to avoid summer heat stress and infestations by the pink bollworm pest.
The Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) is based in Sakrand.

vocab.meaning: growing two or more different crops simultaneously on the same piece of land
relating to the scientific management of land and crop production

text: LAHORE: Pakistan’s cotton and textile supply chain is at a critical juncture, caught between grassroots climate adaptation in the fields of lower Sindh and widening statistical discrepancies in official crop reporting.

The decision by growers in Sindh’s coastal districts of Thatta and Sujawal to begin cotton sowing in the second week of November marks an unusual departure from the country’s conventional agricultural calendar.

However, whether this farmer-led experiment translates into commercial relief for the domestic textile industry depends as much on agronomic resilience through the winter as on resolving data distortions that are currently clouding market pricing.

Traditionally, cotton sowing in Punjab takes place between May and June, while Sindh begins in February and March — a cycle that exposes the crop to peak summer heat stress and post-monsoon pest attacks, particularly from the pink bollworm. By utilising land cleared after the paddy harvest and intercropping directly into standing tomato fields, growers in coastal Sindh are attempting a multi-season model.

Dr Tasawwar Hussain Malik, a plant breeding and genetics specialist at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) in Sakrand, notes that while the initiative originated with farmers, CCRI researchers are closely monitoring the fields and conducting parallel trials to assess the viability of “off-season” planting in frost-free pockets of lower Sindh, where winter temperatures remain comparatively mild.
November sowing in coastal areas could bring early lint supplies, but crop resilience and fibre quality remain uncertain

If the November-sown crop matures through winter and yields lint by February and March, domestic spinners could see fresh arrivals months ahead of the traditional August peak. Such an early injection of raw material would bridge the annual inter-season supply gap and curb reliance on costly imported lint.

For ginning factories, a March start would also extend operational capacity beyond their usual three-to-four-month window, though overlapping with the late wheat harvest could strain local transport, labour and warehousing.
Despite initial optimism, cotton scientists urge caution against declaring November sowing a proven model before the crop completes its full cycle.

Sajid Mahmood, head of technology transfer at CCRI in Multan, points out that while daytime temperatures of 33-34 degrees Celsius and night-time lows of 21-22°C in mid-November appear favourable for germination, air temperature alone does not govern crop success.

Seed germination requires warm soil at seed depth, and the decisive test will arrive between December and February. Falling night and soil temperatures during peak winter can retard root development, delay flowering, and impair boll formation.

Furthermore, prolonged fog, dew, and cool, overly moist soil heighten the risk of the Seedling Disease Complex, driven by soil-borne pathogens such as Rhizoctonia and Pythium, alongside fungal leaf infections.

From an industrial standpoint, sub-optimal winter warmth and reduced sunlight can compromise fibre maturity, lowering micronaire values and staple length. Should early-spring lint fail to meet export-grade spinning specifications, textile mills would inevitably discount the crop, eroding farmer profitability.

Equally concerning is the potential disruption to natural pest cycles. Keeping cotton plants in the ground from November until the conventional spring sowing season could create a continuous green bridge for pink bollworm larvae to multiply and migrate into the main summer crop, he warns, stressing that multi-location comparative trials over at least two to three seasons — tracking soil temperatures, fog days, pest dynamics, and fibre quality alongside strict crop-residue management — are essential before scaling up off-season cultivation.

Compounding these field uncertainties is a stark reporting gap for the 2026-27 season. While the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association recorded Punjab arrivals at 1.999 million bales by Oct 31, the Punjab Crop Reporting Service (CRS) projected provincial output at 3.7m bales, claiming arrivals reached 3.64m bales by Nov 5.

This over 1.6-million-bale discrepancy distorts price discovery across the value chain. Inflated official supply estimates artificially depress local lint prices — currently hovering around Rs18,500 per maund — making growers and ginners hesitant to sell.

Simultaneously, overstated projections risk delaying spinners’ forward import contracts, exposing mills to panic buying on global spot markets at steep premiums if domestic shortfalls emerge, while driving up bank risk premiums and borrowing costs for warehouse financing.

Ultimately, translating coastal Sindh’s November sowing into lasting relief for Pakistan’s textile sector requires institutional alignment: targeted PARC-CCRI seed research for cold-tolerant, pest-resistant varieties paired with credible, unified crop statistics to restore market stability.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Another bullish week as stocks flirt with 180,000-milestone
cards.author: Muhammad Kashif
cards.why: Provides official quarterly and monthly data on fiscal balances, remittance inflows, and equity market trends for economic analysis.
cards.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange recorded a strong weekly advance, briefly crossing the 180,000-point threshold before closing lower on profit-taking. Market sentiment improved following a fall in international crude oil prices, which alleviated fears of imported inflation. Worker remittances expanded substantially during October, bolstering external account inflows. The country also maintained a fiscal surplus during the first quarter of the fiscal year.
key_facts: The KSE-100 index gained 2.29 per cent week-on-week to close at 177,873.88 points after reaching an intra-week high of 180,769.
Remittances sent by overseas Pakistanis reached $3.9 billion in October, bringing cumulative receipts for the first four months of FY27 to $14.8 billion.
Pakistan recorded a first-quarter FY27 fiscal surplus of Rs1,274 billion, representing 0.9 per cent of GDP.
The primary fiscal surplus reached Rs3 trillion during the first quarter of FY27.

vocab.meaning: seeking out and buying stocks that appear underpriced relative to their worth

text: KARACHI: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery rally during the outgoing week as falling international oil prices eased inflation concerns and encouraged value-hunting across the board.

The index crossed the 180,000-point barrier during the second-last trading session but failed to sustain gains as investors resorted to profit-taking. Cautious sentiment amid domestic political uncertainty also capped the rally.

According to Arif Habib Ltd (AHL), the KSE-100 index gained 3,987 points, or 2.29 per cent, week-on-week to close at 177,873.88 points on Friday. It traded between an intra-week high of 180,769 and a low of 176,292 points.

Topline Securities attributed the positive performance primarily to declining crude oil prices and improved investor sentiment amid hopes of a de-escalation in Middle East tensions following the US midterm election results.
Falling oil prices, higher remittances and institutional buying support market

International oil prices retreated sharply during the week, with Brent crude easing to around $96.10 per barrel by Friday. The decline from elevated levels helped ease concerns about imported inflation and the domestic economic outlook.

Among major economic developments, workers’ remittances rose 14pc year-on-year to $3.9 billion in October, compared to $3.4bn in the corresponding month last year. Inflows also increased 8pc month-on-month, taking cumulative remittances during the first four months of FY27 to $14.8bn, up 14pc from a year earlier.

Pakistan posted a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274bn, equivalent to 0.9pc of gross domestic product, during the first quarter of FY27, down 40pc from Rs2,119bn, or 1.7pc of GDP, in the same period last year. The primary surplus stood at Rs3 trillion. Federal Board of Revenue collection amounted to Rs3,086bn, up 7pc year-on-year, while markup payments increased 23pc to Rs1,700bn.

In the latest treasury bill auction, the government raised Rs587bn, exceeding its Rs400bn target, while cut-off yields declined by 22 to 48 basis points across tenors. Meanwhile, central government debt fell 1pc during the first quarter of the current fiscal year to Rs82.7tr as of Sept 30.

The State Bank of Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves increased by $11.3 million to $21.6bn as of Nov 6, while banks’ reserves declined by $37.1m to $5.3bn. Total liquid foreign exchange reserves stood at $26.8bn, providing import cover of approximately three months.
On the energy front, petroleum prices declined by around Rs21 per litre to Rs332 and high-speed diesel by Rs22 to Rs360 per litre.

Weekly oil production edged up 0.5pc to 65,200 barrels per day, while gas output increased 3.3pc to 3,106 million cubic feet per day, supported by higher production from Uch, Kandhkot, Naimat West and Sutiari Deep fields.

Automobile sales also recorded strong growth. Passenger car sales rose sharply in October, with industry data indicating increased demand, particularly for lower-displacement vehicles. The Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association reported sales of 21,635 units, up 60pc year-on-year. The rupee appreciated marginally by 0.02pc against the dollar, closing at Rs276.60 compared to Rs276.66 in the preceding week.

Sector-wise, exploration and production companies led the gains, contributing 1,058 points to the benchmark index, followed by banks with 1,036 points, cement (545 points), fertiliser (317 points) and investment banks (187 points).

Among individual stocks, Mari Petroleum contributed the most, adding 582 points, followed by United Bank (264 points), Lucky Cement (250 points), Pakistan Petroleum (244 points) and Habib Bank (202 points). National Bank led the negative contributors, shedding 48 points, followed by Attock Refinery, Adamjee Insurance, Pakistan Telecommunication and Cnergyico.
AHL expects the market to maintain a cautiously optimistic trajectory, with further gains possible if international oil prices remain stable.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Capital going cashless
cards.author: editorial
cards.why: Directly relevant to questions on economic documentation, digital governance, and financial inclusion barriers in Pakistan.
cards.summary: The federal government aims to make Islamabad Pakistan's first cashless city by December 31, halting cash acceptance at municipal departments from November 30. All merchants are required to adopt digital networks, with priority given to Raast. However, structural challenges such as low banking penetration, gender disparity, and slow internet connections hinder the transition. Heavy reliance on cash persists, with significant currency circulating outside the formal banking system.
key_facts: The government set a deadline of December 31 for Islamabad to become Pakistan's first fully cashless city, halting cash at municipal offices from November 30.
Cash in circulation in Pakistan stands at roughly 34% of GDP, with Rs11.5 trillion held outside the formal banking system.
Only 27% of Pakistani adults possess bank accounts, and just 9% of women made or received a digital payment in the past year.
Nationwide active digital merchants expanded to 2.03 million, with Raast QR codes printed on over 45 million utility bills.

vocab.meaning: continually troubled or distressed by difficulties
growing or developing rapidly

text: The government's decision to make Islamabad Pakistan's first fully cashless city by December 31 is a bold move that suggests either extensive planning or a complete lack of a plan. Starting from November 30, no cash will be accepted at Islamabad Capital Territory or Capital Development Authority departments, and all merchants - from street vendors to business centres - are expected to join digital payment networks, with the priority being on Raast. Some 26,000 merchants are already connected, and nationwide active digital merchants have risen fourfold to 2.03 million, with Raast QR codes printed on more than 45 million utility bills. The government hopes that widespread adoption would help steer the country towards a situation where it can fend off aggression, but success would require many other pieces to fall into place. Notably, despite significant recent improvements, Pakistan remains one of the region's most cash-reliant economies, with cash in circulation at roughly 34% of GDP - more than double the figures for India and Bangladesh - and about Rs11.5 trillion is outside the formal banking system. Only 27% of adults have bank accounts, and just 9% of women made or received a digital payment in the past year. QR codes at every stall do nothing for customers who have no smartphone, no connectivity or no trust in technology. Connectivity is where the biggest problem lies. Pakistan ranks among the lowest 12% globally for mobile and broadband speeds, and average speeds actually fell 40% in 2024. Internet access is still quite low, at around 33%. Islamabad's pilot cashless Sunday bazaar has not inspired much confidence, as it has been plagued by weak signals and patchy connections, with vendors often stepping outside to find reception. Pakistan's burgeoning reputation as a scammers' paradise will also not help earn consumers' or vendors' confidence. Going cashless is a worthwhile goal, but there is no easy route to the destination. Instead of a ridiculously short deadline, the government should first ensure that reliable connectivity, affordable devices, merchant incentives and strong fraud protection are introduced to increase adoption.

cards.title: Running out of gas
cards.author: editorial
cards.why: Essential context for questions on the domestic energy crisis, natural resource depletion, and infrastructure governance.
cards.summary: Pakistan faces a widening natural gas shortage as domestic production has declined by nearly half over the past decade. Sui Southern Gas Company has restricted household gas supply to three mealtime slots per day across Sindh and Balochistan. Low network pressure and the illegal use of suction compressors aggravate supply problems in major urban centres. Imported liquefied natural gas has failed to ensure a steady supply amid regional market disruptions.
key_facts: Pakistan's indigenous natural gas production has fallen by nearly half over the past decade.
Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) restricted domestic gas supply to three scheduled meal times per day in Sindh and Balochistan.
Available natural gas supplies from SSGC dropped by approximately 13% within a single year.

vocab.meaning: originating or occurring naturally in a particular region
severely reduced in quantity or exhausted

text: Pakistan's natural gas reserves have depleted considerably over the years, forcing SSGC to restrict domestic supplies to three designated meal times a day. With indigenous production having declined by nearly half over the past decade, the country is struggling to meet even the basic energy needs of its population. The restrictions have added to the difficulties of households in Sindh and Balochistan, where prolonged outages and low gas pressure have already become commonplace. The problem is particularly acute for urban cities like Karachi, where households already contend with erratic supplies and rising utility bills. Even the assurance of gas during cooking hours offers little relief when pressure is insufficient to operate a stove. The illegal use of suction pumps and compressors, which deprives neighbouring households of their share, is another symptom of a distribution system in which scarcity has become normalised. Consumers should not have to compete for a basic utility, nor should they be expected to bear the consequences of failures in supply management. SSGC's available gas has fallen by almost 13% in a single year, while national production has reportedly halved over the past decade. The disruption of LNG imports from Qatar amid the Middle East conflict has further exposed Pakistan's dependence on external supplies. Yet imported gas has hardly provided a dependable solution. The country has previously struggled with surplus LNG under inflexible contracts, even as domestic shortages persisted. There is no immediate remedy for exhausted gas fields. However, the present shortage demands more than adjustments to household cooking schedules. Scarce supplies must be allocated transparently, losses must be curtailed and investment in domestic production must be encouraged alongside a gradual transition to more sustainable energy sources. Above all, the authorities must recognise that rationing is an emergency measure, not an energy policy.

cards.title: FM Dar calls for stronger regional cooperation as Pakistan hosts ECO ministerial meeting
cards.author: Web Desk
cards.why: Important for evaluating Pakistan's regional multilateral diplomacy and regional trade integration.
cards.summary: Pakistan hosted the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers in Islamabad. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar emphasized greater regional connectivity, economic integration, and trade facilitation across member states. Pakistan outlined the agenda for its upcoming ECO chairmanship under the theme 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO'.
key_facts: Pakistan hosted the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers in Islamabad.
Pakistan's working theme for its incoming ECO chairmanship is 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO'.
Dr Asad Majeed Khan serves as the Secretary General of the Economic Cooperation Organisation.
Pakistan confirmed its plan to host the next ECO summit in 2027.

vocab.meaning: able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions

text: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sunday called for stronger regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration among member states of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) as Pakistan hosted the 30th meeting of the organisation's Council of Ministers in Islamabad. The meeting brought together foreign ministers and senior representatives of member states, as well as regional and international organisations and business leaders, the Foreign Office said. FM Dar discussed Pakistan's priorities for its upcoming ECO chairmanship, themed "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO", with Secretary General Dr Asad Majeed Khan on the sidelines of the meeting, the Foreign Office said in a statement. Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 held a meeting with the Secretary General of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), Dr. Asad Majeed Khan, on the sidelines of the 30th Meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers in Islamabad today.… pic.twitter.com/sZgOMBcMum — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 He also reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to hosting the ECO summit in 2027. Dr Majeed appreciated Pakistan's arrangements, hospitality and coordination for the ministerial meeting while congratulating the country on its upcoming chairmanship and plans to host the ECO Council of Ministers meeting and summit in 2027. FM Dar appreciated the ECO Secretariat's efforts to advance the organisation's agenda and its support for Pakistan's priorities during its chairmanship. Both sides stressed the importance of close coordination to ensure the effective implementation of agreed initiatives and advance shared objectives of regional development and prosperity. The conference is expected to highlight Pakistan's role as a regional connectivity hub, particularly through initiatives such as the proposed Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan railway project and expanding trade links with Central Asian states. Building on bilateral trade agreements with Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, Pakistan plans to engage ECO partners on measures to expand commerce, improve transit arrangements and strengthen regional supply chains. Meetings with CICA, OIC officials Separately, FM Dar met the Secretary General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev. During the meeting, FM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's support for CICA and its efforts to promote peace, security and stability in Asia through dialogue and confidence-building measures. He also welcomed the successful convening of the organisation's seventh summit in Baku under Azerbaijan's chairmanship. Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 held a meeting with the Secretary General of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev, on the sidelines of the 30th Meeting of the ECO… pic.twitter.com/ppsyIJUJwr — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 Hajiyev appreciated Pakistan's efforts and constructive role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation, and thanked the country for its hospitality and arrangements for the ECO ministerial meeting. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation within CICA to advance regional peace and prosperity. According to FO, senior officials from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkiye, along with representatives of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), arrived in Islamabad to attend the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting. The FO said Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan Elnur Mammadov, who is also heading his country's delegation, had "arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting". He was received at Islamabad International Airport by FO officials. H.E. Mr. Elnur Mammadov, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Head of Delegation, arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting. He was received at Islamabad International Airport by the officers of MoFA. pic.twitter.com/ZOeEOVAHpd — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 Deputy Secretary General of the SCO Ahmad Saidmurodzoda also arrived to attend the meeting and was received by FO officials, according to another post. Mr. Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Deputy Secretary General of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting. He was received at Islamabad International Airport by the officers of MoFA. #ECOCOM30th… pic.twitter.com/05u34AKUIg — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 The FO said Kazakhstan's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arman Issagaliyev, who is heading his country's delegation, had also arrived in Islamabad for the meeting. He was received at the airport by ministry officials. H.E. Mr. Arman Issagaliyev, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan and Head of Delegation, arrived in Islamabad for the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting. He was received at Islamabad International Airport by officials of MoFA. #ECOCOM30th… pic.twitter.com/DzBMdQxvZS — Ministry of Foreign Affairs - Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) November 15, 2026 The two-day meeting is being held in Islamabad on November 15 and 16 under the chairmanship of FM Dar. It will bring together foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, alongside representatives of the organisation's secretariat and subsidiary bodies. The ministerial meeting will be preceded by a gathering of senior officials from member states, who will review the organisation's activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation's objectives under the theme "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO". The ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkiye and expanded in 1992 to include Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. The 10-member regional organisation aims to promote economic development through cooperation in areas including trade, transport, energy and investment.

cards.title: Turkiye approves Makkah defence pact
cards.author: Anadolu Agency
cards.why: Highly relevant for Pakistan's strategic alliances, Middle East diplomacy, and collective security agreements.
cards.summary: The Turkish parliament ratified the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, publishing the legislation in its Official Gazette. The bill passed with 279 affirmative votes in the Turkish legislature. Originally signed on August 7, the trilateral pact commits the three countries to collective security and deeper defense cooperation.
key_facts: The Turkish parliament approved the ratification of the trilateral Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence with 279 votes to 119.
The Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey on August 7.
The pact legally came into force in Turkey immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette.

vocab.meaning: formal approval or confirmation making a treaty officially valid

text: A law approving Türkiye's ratification of a joint defence agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia was published on Saturday in the country's Official Gazette The law covers the "Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence Between the Republic of Türkiye, the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," signed in Makkah on August 7. Under the legislation, the law takes effect upon publication. Turkish parliament approved the measure with 279 votes to 119 on November 5. A total of 398 lawmakers participated in the vote in the 592-member parliament. Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement during a trilateral summit in the holy city on Aug 7. Under the agreement, the three countries pledged to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

cards.title: Thousands rally in Antalya to demand climate justice as COP31 talks hit midpoint
cards.author: AFP, News Desk
cards.why: Important context for essays and questions on multilateral climate treaties, developing-country financing, and COP summit outcomes.
cards.summary: Over 7,000 environmental demonstrators marched through Antalya as the COP31 global climate summit entered its halfway point. Protesters condemned the lack of progress on phasing out fossil fuels and securing adaptation funding for vulnerable societies. Turkiye faced scrutiny for continuing to develop coal infrastructure despite serving as conference co-chair. Diplomats from approximately two hundred countries are working toward a negotiated agreement before the summit finishes.
key_facts: The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) took place in Antalya, Turkiye.
Negotiators representing roughly 200 countries participated in the summit.
More than 7,000 people took part in the central demonstration organised by the People's Climate Summit platform.

vocab.meaning: a deceptive outward appearance that conceals reality

cards.title: Goods exports rise 8.8pc to record $11.4b in first four months of FY27
cards.author: Web Desk
cards.why: Provides official trade statistics useful for macroeconomic analysis and balance of payments questions.
cards.summary: Pakistan's merchandise exports grew 8.8% to reach a record $11.4 billion during the first four months of fiscal year 2026-27. The increase followed policy support, including tax cuts, expedited refund processing, and subsidized SME financing. The rebound follows an export contraction in fiscal year 2025-26, when outbound shipments dropped to $30.8 billion amid agricultural losses and regional conflicts.
key_facts: Pakistan's goods exports reached a record $11.4 billion during July-October of FY 2026-27, rising 8.8% year-on-year from $10.4 billion.
Annual goods exports in FY 2025-26 contracted to $30.8 billion from $32.04 billion in FY 2024-25.
The previous year's trade contraction was partly caused by a $1 billion drop in rice shipments and regional conflict disruptions.

vocab.meaning: making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible

cards.title: Middle power aspirations
cards.author: Khurram Abbas
cards.why: Offers useful conceptual framing for International Relations essays on multipolarity and middle power diplomacy.
cards.summary: As global power structures shift away from unipolarity toward fragmented multipolarity, middle powers serve as vital diplomatic bridges and trade stabilizers. Scholars judge middle power status using three primary criteria: military strength, diplomatic engagement, and overall national capacity. While countries like Turkey, South Korea, and Australia rely on distinct strengths, Pakistan has boosted its security profile and diplomatic activity. However, Pakistan's standing is constrained because its underlying economic and technological foundations remain fragile.
key_facts: Scholars evaluate middle power status across three core pillars: military capability, diplomatic outreach, and comprehensive national strength.
Comprehensive national strength is primarily defined by economic vitality and technological adaptation.

vocab.meaning: the division of something into two branches or opposing parts

cards.title: Judges must speak
cards.why: Useful for essays on judicial reform, institutional accountability, and legal ethics in Pakistan.
cards.summary: Judicial authority is strengthened rather than harmed by open critique from the legal academy, bar, and public. In Pakistan, retired judges seldom publicly discuss their past decisions, creating an absence of institutional accountability and educational reflection. A former Supreme Court justice argues that retired judges should visit law colleges and openly assess their past rulings, including acknowledging mistakes. Transparent public engagement by former judges could deter sitting benches from bending legal principles to appease power.
key_facts: In the 2023 Supreme Court case concerning provincial assembly elections in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the outcome was interpreted as a four-to-three split by dissenting judges.

vocab.meaning: the quality of being open, sincere, and honest in speech

cards.title: Asif hopeful of consensus on new provinces, says it will bring 'progressive' change in political landscape
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: The creation of administrative units and federal restructuring are recurring themes in Pakistan Affairs and Governance papers.
cards.summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif stated that consultative efforts are progressing toward building a national consensus on creating new provinces. He noted that reorganising administrative units could progressively reshape Pakistan's political landscape. Consultations between the president and prime minister affirmed that any restructuring must follow strict constitutional provisions.
key_facts: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif announced that political consultations have been ongoing to establish a consensus on creating new provinces.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed the need to strictly adhere to constitutional procedures governing new administrative units.

vocab.meaning: a general agreement among a group of people
to closely follow or observe a rule or standard

cards.title: Blasts rattle Bahrain as Iran launches second drone attack in 3 days
cards.author: AFP
cards.why: Important for tracking regional conflict dynamics, proxy warfare, and security vulnerabilities in the Persian Gulf.
cards.summary: Bahrain's air defence systems intercepted an Iranian drone strike aimed at a US military installation. The attack targeted a radar facility at the Al-Riffa helicopter base, marking the second such assault in three days. The strikes disrupted a quiet period across the Gulf amid wider regional conflict.
key_facts: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain.
Bahrain hosts major US military facilities in the Persian Gulf, including a naval base.

vocab.meaning: stopped or seized something before it arrived at its destination
a temporary period of calm or quiet

mcqs.q: According to the results of the 2023 national census, what was Pakistan's annual population growth rate?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan's 2023 census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55 percent, exerting heavy pressure on resources and social services. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: Under Pakistan's National Finance Commission (NFC) formula, what percentage weight is allocated to population in the distribution of federal resources to provinces?
mcqs.explanation: The NFC formula assigns an 82 percent weight to population size, which has drawn scrutiny for potentially disincentivizing provincial birth control measures. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: In which month and year was the 26th Constitutional Amendment enacted in Pakistan, which originally created constitutional benches within the Supreme Court?
mcqs.explanation: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024, introducing constitutional benches whose members were selected by a restructured Judicial Commission. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: Where did the Global Organised Crime Index 2025 rank Pakistan out of a total of 193 evaluated countries?
mcqs.explanation: The Global Organised Crime Index 2025 placed Pakistan in the 45th position among 193 nations. [Dawn]

mcqs.explanation: The 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report released by the US State Department placed Pakistan on Tier 2. [Dawn]

mcqs.explanation: The Simla Conference took place in 1913-14, where British India and Tibetan envoys signed an agreement setting the McMahon Line as the border, without Chinese consent. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: Which city hosted the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers in November 2026?

mcqs.q: How many member states currently constitute the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO)?
mcqs.explanation: The ECO consists of 10 member states: Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic, and Uzbekistan. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: The annual report titled 'The 500 Most Influential Muslims' is compiled and published by a research institute located in which country?
mcqs.explanation: The Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), which publishes the ranking annually, is based in Amman, Jordan. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, highlighted in late 2026, formed a trilateral mutual defence alliance among which nations?
mcqs.explanation: The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is a collective defence pact uniting Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, an Iranian drone attack targeted a US air defence radar system located at which site in Bahrain?
mcqs.explanation: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, which group of five European nations was chosen at a meeting in Dublin to send envoys to future talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war?
options: France, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, and Poland
France, Germany, Spain, Poland, and Sweden
The United Kingdom, Germany, Norway, Italy, and Finland
France, Italy, Poland, the Netherlands, and Turkey

mcqs.q: According to official data reported in November 2026, how much did workers' remittances to Pakistan total during October?
mcqs.explanation: Remittances reached $3.9 billion in October, taking cumulative receipts for the first four months of FY27 to $14.8 billion. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: What was Pakistan's fiscal surplus as a percentage of gross domestic product during the first quarter of FY27?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan recorded a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274 billion, or 0.9 per cent of GDP, in the first quarter of FY27. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: Which city hosted the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Antalya in Turkiye served as the host city for the COP31 climate negotiations. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: The Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) tracking off-season winter cotton trials in Sindh is situated in which town?
mcqs.explanation: The Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) is located in Sakrand, where researchers are monitoring experimental off-season cotton planting. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: Under the federal government's digital economy initiative in November 2026, which city was set a deadline of December 31 to become Pakistan's first fully cashless city?
mcqs.explanation: The government announced that Islamabad will transition into Pakistan's first fully cashless city by December 31, halting cash transactions at municipal departments from November 30. [The Express Tribune]

mcqs.q: What is the theme of Pakistan's chairmanship of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) announced at the 30th Council of Ministers meeting?

Building Strategic Infrastructure and Energy Security

mcqs.q: Who served as the Secretary General of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) during its ministerial meeting held in Islamabad in November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Former Pakistani diplomat Dr Asad Majeed Khan served as the Secretary General of the Economic Cooperation Organisation. [The Express Tribune]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, the parliament of which country ratified the trilateral Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia?
mcqs.explanation: The Turkish parliament approved the ratification of the trilateral Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence between Turkiye, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia by a 279-119 vote. [The Express Tribune]
